One of the key challenges is accurate diagnosis. Cellulitis remains a clinical diagnosis without a validated diagnostic test, so misdiagnosis is common, with approximately 40% of patients eventually receiving an alternative diagnosis.2 Clinicians might default to a diagnosis of cellulitis when presented with an erythematous lower limb because alternative diagnoses are less familiar.3 The linked practice pointer by Yadav and colleagues (doi:10.1136/bmj-2026-100505) gives a practical diagnostic approach.4 Key mimics include stasis dermatitis, eczema, and oedema or lymphoedema; these conditions might coexist with cellulitis, which compounds the uncertainty of diagnosis.

This decision has become increasingly difficult as transplant programmes consider older and more medically complex candidates and use more kidneys from older donors or after circulatory death.12 A linked study (doi:10.1136/bmj-2026-100624) aims to reduce this uncertainty by using registry data from 64 035 waitlisted dialysis patients across five European registries.3 The authors emulated 60 sequential monthly trials, comparing transplantation during a given month with remaining waitlisted on dialysis during that month.

world.summary: A new technical brief calls for more consistent and rigorous measurement of non-partner sexual violence against women and girls – a widespread form of violence that remains underreported and inadequately measured.Non-partner sexual violence, defined as sexual violence perpetrated by someone other than an intimate partner – is a global public health and human rights issue with serious consequences for women’s physical, mental, sexual and reproductive health. An estimated 263 million women and girls aged 15 years and older, or 8% globally, have been subjected to sexual violence from a man other than an intimate partner at least once since the age of 15 years. The prevalence is likely to be much higher because of gaps in available evidence, measurement challenges and the underreporting associated with stigma and fear of repercussions.The new brief by the UNDP/UNFPA/UNICEF/WHO/World Bank Special Programme of Research, Development and Research Training in Human Reproduction (HRP), the World Health Organization (WHO) and United Nations partners, identifies key measurement challenges and provides recommendations to researchers, statistical offices and others designing population-based surveys for strengthening the measurement of non-partner sexual violence.Where are the gaps?WHO’s review of population-based surveys, conducted between 2000 and 2023, identified 140 countries with at least one eligible survey, covering 89% of the global population of women and girls aged 15 years and older.

epidemiology.title: Translating evidence to action: One year of postpartum haemorrhage guideline implementation - World Health Organization (WHO)
epidemiology.summary: In 2026, postpartum haemorrhage (PPH) remains a leading cause of maternal mortality globally, underscoring the urgent need for sustained action across all levels of healthcare systems. One year after the publication and landmark launch of the WHO-FIGO-ICM Consolidated guidelines for the prevention, diagnosis and treatment of PPH at the XXV FIGO World Congress in Cape Town, this World PPH Day webinar will convene global experts to reflect on progress, share implementation experiences and accelerate action to reduce the burden of PPH worldwide.Led by FIGO in collaboration with HRP (the UNDP/UNFPA/UNICEF/WHO/World Bank Special Programme of Research, Development and Research Training in Human Reproduction), the World Health Organization (WHO) and the International Confederation of Midwives (ICM), this session will examine how countries, professional societies, healthcare providers and partners are translating evidence into practice. Speakers will provide updates on progress against the Roadmap to Combat Postpartum Haemorrhage between 2023 and 2030, highlight the new implementation guide published earlier this year and share lessons learned from implementing the guidelines across diverse health system contexts.Drawing on the perspectives of leaders from international organisations, the frontlines of obstetrics and midwifery, and national ministries of health, presentations will showcase real-world implementation experiences and outcomes, spotlighting successes, challenges and transferable strategies for improving PPH prevention, diagnosis and treatment.Following an audience Q&A, this webinar will conclude with a renewed call to action for FIGO's member societies and partners to advocate for the review and adaptation of the guidelines at the national level, support the implementation and uptake of updated PPH guidance, strengthen healthcare workforce capabilities and foster collaboration across disciplines and sectors to drive collective action in the fight against PPH.Register for the webinar today and join the global movement translating evidence into action to end preventable maternal deaths from PPH: https://figo.ooo/46bOut1.

clinical_trials.title: Gut Viruses May Warn of Deadly Intestinal Disease in Preemies Up to Eight Days Early - trialsitenews.com
clinical_trials.summary: Kailun Zhang, PhD, of Washington University School of Medicine in St. Louis, and colleagues report in Gut that microbial signatures in premature infants may predict necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC) up to eight days before symptoms. Analyzing 1,825 longitudinal stool samples from 43 infants who developed NEC and 86 gestational-age- and birthweight-matched controls, researchers found that phage-bacterial signatures predicted early-onset NEC with 75% accuracy and 81% sensitivity, while bacterial antibiotic-resistance profiles predicted late-onset NEC with 83% accuracy.

clinical_trials.title: Mindfulness and Tai Chi Ease Fatigue and Pain After Cancer—but Benefits Are Modest - trialsitenews.com
clinical_trials.summary: Yan Ma, PhD, of the Osher Center for Integrative Health at Harvard Medical School and Brigham and Women’s Hospital, with lead investigator Linda Carlson, PhD, University of Calgary, and colleagues report in the Journal of Clinical Oncology that mindfulness-based cancer recovery (MBCR) and Tai Chi/Qigong (TCQ) reduced fatigue and pain interference among distressed cancer survivors. In the 587-person MATCH trial, TCQ also improved sleep quality. The findings support mind-body therapies as potentially useful supportive care—but they did not substantially reduce pain intensity, an important distinction between feeling less pain and functioning better despite it.

clinical_trials.title: Boston Children’s Maps New Pathways Behind Dangerous Heart Scarring in HLHS—but ‘Breakthrough’ Needs Perspective - trialsitenews.com
clinical_trials.summary: Boston Children’s Hospital researchers have produced a sharper molecular map of endocardial fibroelastosis (EFE), severe cardiac fibrosis frequently associated with hypoplastic left heart syndrome (HLHS). Published as a research letter in Circulation, the work identifies distinct abnormal states of endothelial cells—cells lining blood vessels—and signaling pathways that could eventually become therapeutic targets. But Boston Children’s description of the research as a “breakthrough” deserves context: this is sophisticated, early-stage mechanistic research involving very few human tissue samples, not evidence of a new treatment.
